tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Brahim's headline, summary, location, languages, certifications (with verification links), skills and links. Start here.

tools.name: get_availability
tools.description: Whether Brahim is open to new roles right now, what kind, from when, and where (dated).

tools.name: list_items
tools.description: List the anonymised client case studies (work), side projects (projects) or technical notes (notes), newest first, with a one-line summary and URL.

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: Full text (Markdown) of one case study, project or note by its slug, as listed by list_items. Case studies and projects also exist in French.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Keyword search across every case study, project and note (e.g. "DataWeave", "CCv2 migration", "MCP"). Returns titles, URLs and a snippet; use get_item for the full text.

tools.name: request_cv
tools.description: File a request for Brahim's full CV, exactly like the form on heybrahim.com/cv.html. Brahim reads every request and sends the CV himself by email, usually the same day; nothing is sent automatically. Only call this when the user explicitly asked for the CV and gave their own name and email. Limited

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_items, search · Private data: request_cv · Public sink: request_cv.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_items, search · Private data: request_cv · Public sink: request_cv

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
